intro.title: Path, URL & OS
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js script that uses built-in modules to work with file paths, URLs, and operating system information. You'll learn how to manipulate and join file paths, parse URL components, and retrieve system details like the platform and memory. The core programming concept is using Node.js's standard library modules—specifically 'path', 'url', and 'os'—to handle common system-level tasks. This will help you understand how Node.js interacts with the underlying environment, a key skill for backend development. By the end, you'll have a script that demonstrates practical examples of these modules in action.
intro.usecase: The Path, URL, and OS modules are foundational for building file-based applications and web servers in Node.js. For example, a developer might use the Path module to resolve file upload locations in a dashboard's media management panel, ensuring cross-platform compatibility. The URL module is essential for parsing query parameters in a search or filter interface, while the OS module helps monitor server health metrics displayed in an admin console. These tools are critical for creating robust, production-ready applications that handle files, network requests, and system resources effectively.
